caption:
Two people, one tape.
Both are listening to the same music.

Now one of them wants to say something.
How do you talk with your headphones still on?
Sony released its first Walkman in 1979.

It was a portable cassette player
with a pair of lightweight headphones.

Look at the two cords.
Each pair of headphones had its own jack.

In 1981, Sony’s Akio Morita
wrote about testing an early model.

Listening at home, he had an idea.
A second pair of headphones would let someone listen along.

Later, he took the player on a drive
with his friend Kaoru Shoji.

Morita had brought a tape of Shoji’s wife,
Hiroko Nakamura, playing the piano.

There they were, side by side,
listening to her play.

Whenever they wanted to talk, Morita recalled,
the headphones had to come off.

So he asked for a button that would switch on
a microphone inside the player.

With the button down, the person beside you
could hear your voice through their headphones.
Sony called it the Hot Line.
